title: November Examination
instructions: This paper consists of FOUR questions. Answer ALL the questions.
Show all calculations and include units.
Write in full sentences where explanations are required.

questions.prompt: Lines of longitude measure distance…
options: north and south of the equator
east and west of the Prime Meridian

questions.prompt: Which instrument measures air pressure?
Which climate region has hot, dry summers and wet winters?
A settlement where buildings are spread far apart is…
Which type of transport is best for exporting large amounts of coal to China?
Places east of the Prime Meridian are ahead of Greenwich time.
A small-scale map shows a small area in great detail.
What is the line of latitude at 23½° S called?
Which zone of a city has the tallest buildings and highest land values? (give the abbreviation)
Match each term to its meaning.

pairs.right: Growth of the urban share of population

questions.prompt: On a 1 : 50 000 topographic map, two dams are 7,2 cm apart. Calculate the real distance in km.
What is the bearing of south-west?
It is 09:00 at Greenwich (0°). Calculate the time at 75° E. Show your working.
questions.memo:
✓ 75 ÷ 15 = 5 hours (1)
✓ East is ahead, so add (1)
✓ 09:00 + 5 h = 14:00 (1)

questions.prompt: How would you know from contour lines that a slope is steep?
questions.memo:
✓ The contour lines are close together (1)
✓ meaning height changes quickly over a short distance (1)

questions.prompt: Pretoria is at 25°45′ S, 28°11′ E. In which two hemispheres is Pretoria?
Calculate the annual temperature range of Town X.
In which month does Town X receive the most rain? (write the month in full)
Name the climate region of Town X and give TWO reasons from the data.
questions.memo:
✓ Mediterranean (1)
✓ Most rain falls in winter (May to August) (1)
✓ Warm summers and mild winters (1)

questions.prompt: Explain how ocean currents affect the climates of the east and west coasts of South Africa.
questions.memo:
✓ The warm Agulhas Current on the east coast brings warm, moist air and rain (1)
✓ The cold Benguela Current on the west coast cools the air (1)
✓ so the west coast is dry / desert (1)

questions.prompt: Explain why a coastal town has a smaller temperature range than an inland town.
questions.memo:
✓ The sea heats up and cools down slowly (1)
✓ so it keeps coastal temperatures mild in summer and winter (1)

questions.prompt: Give TWO push factors and TWO pull factors that cause rural–urban migration.
questions.memo:
Push (1 each): lack of jobs; drought; poverty; few services; conflict
Pull (1 each): jobs; better services; education; healthcare; family; bright lights

questions.prompt: Describe TWO problems caused by rapid urbanisation and suggest a solution for each.
questions.memo:
✓ Problem 1 (1) ✓ matching solution (1)
✓ Problem 2 (1) ✓ matching solution (1)
e.g. housing shortage → housing programmes; congestion → public transport; unemployment → support small businesses

questions.prompt: Compare road and rail transport by giving ONE advantage of each and stating which is better for moving iron ore.
questions.memo:
✓ Road: door-to-door / flexible (1)
✓ Rail: carries heavy loads cheaply (1)
✓ Rail is better for iron ore (1)

questions.prompt: A country exports goods worth R240 billion and imports goods worth R260 billion. Calculate the balance of trade in billions of rand (use a minus sign for a deficit).
Why do developing countries earn less from exporting raw materials than from manufactured goods?
questions.memo:
✓ Raw materials have a lower value than processed goods (1)
✓ The value is added (and jobs created) in the countries that manufacture the products (1)
